subject: Performance discovery: latency & streaming posture — recap and actions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@lumeninc.com>, Sophia Rivera <sophia.rivera@lumeninc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Performance discovery: latency & streaming posture — recap and actions

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap of the performance posture we discussed and proposed next steps so we have a single MAP to move to a pilot decision.

Summary of the ask (from Amit):
- Hard latency per-user SLO: 95th <= 250ms for short completions (~<80 tokens)
- Streaming target for real-time transcripts: end-to-end initial token <= 120ms, sustained streaming throughput 50 concurrent streams
- Burst throughput: support 600 qps sustained on peak (non-streaming), with graceful degradation to cheaper model variant

What we showed:
- Redwood hosted can meet 250ms 95p at ~120 qps with model X-XL (quantized) in our demo rig; with batching and KV caching we can increase throughput at modest latency cost
- For streaming we showed continuous batching and prefix-KV cache to reduce redundant compute across clients when they reuse contexts

Immediate next items (proposed MAP):
1) LumenInc to share a 24-hour representative traffic trace (qps, request size distribution, percent streaming) by 2028-07-04 — Amit
2) Redwood to run a targeted nvbench profile based on the trace and return a draft SLO checklist + cost estimate by 2028-07-06 — Jordan/Karthik
3) Technical deep-dive (1hr) on streaming tokenization and client latency with your SREs — tentatively 2028-07-08 — Sophia/Soojin to coordinate
4) Contract/pricing signal: if results align, propose a pilot commit (3 months, reserved capacity) — commercial check after nvbench

Attachments: demo recording, draft SLO checklist (attached), sample nvbench log for the demo run.

Open questions for your team:
- Are your streaming sessions long-lived (minutes) or short bursts (<30s) on average?
- Do you have hard concurrency caps per-user or per-API key we should be aware of?

Thanks — I'll kick off the nvbench run as soon as we have the trace.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]

---
Note: attachments referenced above: demo-recording-20280701.mp4, slo-checklist-draft.xlsx, nvbench-sample-log.txt
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@lumeninc.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sophia Rivera <sophia.rivera@lumeninc.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance discovery: latency & streaming posture — recap and actions

Jordan — thanks for the succinct recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming sessions are mixed: ~60% are short (10–30s) for quick voice notes, 40% are 1–10 minutes for live dictation.
- Average token length per request is ~40 tokens; spikes to 300 tokens are rare but exist (less than 0.5% of traffic).
- Concurrency: we currently target 150 concurrent streaming sessions in production; bursts can reach 400 during peak events (we expect that 600 qps non-streaming is an upper bound for a marketing spike).

We will upload a scrubbed 24-hour trace to the Drive link you shared by end of day 2028-07-03. Also tagging Sophia (SRE) to join the deep-dive — she has some packet capture data that may help latency root-cause analysis.

Two asks back to Redwood: 
1) Please include a run with a warmed KV cache scenario in the nvbench profile (we expect many repeated prefixes).
2) Can you provide a cost delta if we use model X-Lite for fallback on degraded days? Even rough $/1M tokens estimate will help internal stakeholding.

Appreciate it,
Amit
Product Lead, LumenInc
amit.shah@lumeninc.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@lumeninc.com>, Sophia Rivera <sophia.rivera@lumeninc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance discovery: latency & streaming posture — recap and actions

Thanks Amit — that breakdown is perfect and helps shape the nvbench profile. Actions updated below: 

- Jordan/Karthik: include warmed and cold-KV cache runs; three scenarios for streaming: 50, 150, 400 concurrent streams; measure p50/p95 initial-token latency and steady-state tail. Deliverable: nvbench artifacts + SLO checklist with recommended thresholds. (Due 2028-07-06)
- Jordan: include cost delta for model X-Lite fallback (rough $/1M tokens and projected monthly spend for pilot traffic)
- Sophia & LumenInc SRE: share any packet-capture latency points + the scrubbed 24-hour trace into the Drive folder by 2028-07-03
- Soojin/Karthik: propose a short technical agenda for the 2028-07-08 deep-dive (30–45m) — include client SDK handshake and tokenization behavior

I'll attach the nvbench run summary once it completes. If there are any contractual constraints (SLA, data retention), flag them now so we can line up security/compliance early.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: nvbench plan + deep-dive agenda (prep)

Internal note — tracking the items Jordan outlined. Quick internal checklist before the deep-dive: 

- nvbench scenarios to run: 1) non-streaming 50/150/600 qps, 2) streaming 50/150/400 concurrent streams, 3) warmed vs cold KV cache across both profiles.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95 initial-token latency, sustained throughput, GPU util, mem pressure, token-per-second per-GPU, and tail CPU steal events.
- Cost delta calc: run X-Lite at same profiles and capture token-costs + expected request mix; produce simple table (pilot-month, projected tokens, estimated $).
- Deliverables: nvbench artifacts (logs, csv), summary slides (one-pager), SLO checklist XLSX, and a short Ops runbook for degradation fallback.

I'll prepare the technical agenda:
- 10m: quick LumenInc topology + client handshake
- 15m: nvbench findings and live-run of 2 scenarios
- 10m: fallback model behavior and cost tradeoffs
- 10m: actions & go/no-go criteria for pilot

Assigning owners: Karthik will run nvbench on our staging with the trace; I'll assemble the slides and the XLSX SLO checklist.

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
